content.title: About
content.content: Spinach, frozen, cooked, fat added is a ready‑to‑eat vegetable that has been blanched, flash‑frozen and enriched with plant or animal fat to improve flavor and texture. It is commonly used as a quick ingredient for side dishes, soups, casseroles and stir‑fries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach belongs to the Amaranthaceae family and is considered one of the most nutrient‑dense leafy greens.
Freezing preserves most of its vitamins, especially vitamin C and folate.
Added fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E and K found in spinach.
Spinach is often used as a base for baby foods because of its soft texture after cooking.
In the United States and Canada, spinach is frequently sold as a ready‑mix for pasta, pizza and other convenience meals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Spinach provides lutein, zeaxanthin and vitamin C, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin help maintain retinal health and reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Source of iron and calcium
items.content: Spinach supplies plant‑based iron and calcium important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Improved vitamin absorption thanks to fat
items.content: The added fat allows the body to better absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: Spinach is rich in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processing may include added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Allergy to added fats
items.content: If animal‑derived fat is used, individuals with dairy or animal fat allergies should be cautious.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the spinach in the microwave or a skillet, stir it into soups, stews, pasta, omelets, or use it as a filling for pies and quiches. It is convenient in portioned bags for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen spinach at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
